chapters.1.lds: Why does receiving Onesimus as Paul himself make partnership costly?
chapters.1.summary: Paul, a prisoner, writes with Timothy to Philemon and the assembly in his house. Paul thanks God for Philemon’s love and faith. He could command, but he appeals out of love. He appeals for Onesimus, who became his child during his imprisonment. Paul sends him back and calls him his own heart. He asks Philemon to receive him as a beloved brother, more than a slave. Paul will repay anything Onesimus owes. He asks for a guest room and sends greetings.
